author: Mohammad Yeasin
subject: grammar
title: Present Perfect Continuous Tense
intro_blurb: The Present Perfect Continuous Tense is used to describe actions that started in the past and are still continuing in the present, often with a focus on the duration. It is heavily used in IELTS Speaking and Writing to describe experiences and ongoing situations. In this lesson, you will learn the rules, Bangla explanation, examples, common mistakes, and practice exercises.
learning_outcomes: Understand when to use the Present Perfect Continuous
Form sentences with have/has + been + verb-ing
Distinguish between Present Perfect and Present Perfect Continuous

timeline.description: I have been living in Dhaka for 5 years. (Started in the past, still living now)

comparison.usage: Focuses on the duration of the action
comparison.example: I have been reading for 2 hours.

comparison.usage: Focuses on the result or completion of the action

common_mistakes.wrong: I have been know him for years.
common_mistakes.right: I have known him for years.
common_mistakes.explanation: Stative verbs (like 'know', 'like', 'belong') cannot be used in continuous tenses.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have been work here since 2020.
common_mistakes.right: I have been working here since 2020.

audio_examples: I have been learning English for three years.
She has been working at the bank since 2020.
They have been playing cricket all afternoon.
speaking_practice: I have been living in Dhaka for 10 years.
She has been studying English since 2022.
They have been waiting for the bus for 30 minutes.
Have you been working here long?
He has not been feeling well lately.

quiz.question: Choose the correct time expression for a duration.
quiz.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration (e.g., 2 hours, 5 years). 'Since' is used with a starting point.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: I _____ (wait) for you since 10 am.
Correct the sentence: He have been working here since 2020.
quiz.answer: He has been working here since 2020.

quiz.question: Translate to English: আমি তিন বছর ধরে ইংরেজি শিখছি।
quiz.answer: I have been learning English for three years.

faq.q: When do we use the Present Perfect Continuous?
faq.a: For actions that started in the past and continue to the present, especially when we want to emphasize the duration.

faq.q: What is the difference between 'for' and 'since'?
faq.a: 'For' is used with a duration (e.g., 3 years, 2 hours). 'Since' is used with a starting point (e.g., 2020, Monday).

faq.q: What is the difference between Present Perfect and Present Perfect Continuous?
faq.a: Present Perfect focuses on the result; Present Perfect Continuous focuses on the duration of the action.

faq.q: Can I use this tense with stative verbs?
faq.a: No. Stative verbs (like know, be, have, like) cannot be used in continuous forms. Use Present Perfect instead.
